chunks: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled that the 'mudabbir' (a slave manumitted upon the owner's death) is entitled to one-third of the estate, and that a man may revoke his will, adding to it or subtracting from it, as long as he has not died.

key_terms.اَلْمُدَبَّر: A slave manumitted upon the owner's death, entitled to a specific share of the estate

ai.seo_question: What is the share of a mudabbir in inheritance and can a person change their will before dying?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) juristic authority in defining the status of the *mudabbir* (manumission-deferred slave) as entitled to one-third of the estate, a key concept in Shia inheritance law. It further establishes the principle of *ruju'* (revocability) in wills, affirming that a testator retains full autonomy to alter or revoke their testamentary dispositions prior to death, provided they are still alive.
